title: Optimistic updates and rollback
description: Learn how optimistic updates improve perceived performance and when rollback strategies are needed. This lesson covers implementation patterns with React Query and how to handle failures gracefully.

data.text: Optimistic updates are changes to the UI that are applied before the server confirms they are permanent. When the user clicks "Like", the heart icon turns red instantly instead of waiting for the API call to finish. If the request fails, the UI rolls back to the previous state.

Done well, optimistic updates make an application feel fast. Done poorly, they create confusing UI states and data loss. This lesson teaches you how to implement optimistic updates safely and how to design rollback behavior that keeps users informed.

Network requests are unpredictable. On a fast connection, a mutation may complete in 50 milliseconds; on a slow network, it may take several seconds. By updating the UI immediately, you hide the network latency from the user. Studies consistently show that perceived responsiveness matters more than raw speed.

data.title: Good candidates for optimistic updates
items: Archiving or deleting a row from a list
Updating a todo item in place
Switching tabs or toggling a setting

data.text: Implementing optimistic updates with React Query

React Query supports optimistic updates through the `onMutate` callback. Inside `onMutate`, you snapshot the current cache, apply the optimistic change, and return a context object. If the mutation fails, the `onError` callback uses the snapshot to roll back. On success, `onSettled` refetches to ensure the cache matches the server.

data.title: Optimistic like with rollback
data.content: The mutation updates the UI immediately, rolls back on failure, and refetches on success.

data.text: Rollback is not simply reverting the cache. A good rollback experience also tells the user what happened and what they can do next. If the mutation fails, show a non-blocking toast notification with the error and a retry button. Do not silently undo the user's action; they may believe it succeeded.

data.title: Rollback UX checklist
items: Show a visible error message when the optimistic update fails.
Keep the rollback undoable by offering a retry action.
Use `isPending` from the mutation to disable repeated clicks while the request is in flight.
Avoid optimistic updates for critical financial or irreversible actions unless the risk of failure is extremely low.

data.title: When to avoid optimistic updates
data.text: Do not use optimistic updates for operations that cannot be safely reversed, such as payments, account deletion, or sending an email. For these actions, show a loading state until the server confirms success.

Not every mutation needs an optimistic update. In some cases, a simple loading state is clearer and less error-prone. Choose pessimistic updates when the action is destructive, when validation on the server is expensive, or when the UI would be confusing if rolled back.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: Optimistic updates improve perceived performance by applying changes before the server responds.
Always pair optimistic updates with rollback, error messaging, and retry options.
React Query provides first-class support for optimistic updates via `onMutate`, `onError`, and `onSettled`.
Use pessimistic updates for irreversible or high-stakes actions.
data.takeaway: Optimistic updates are a UX pattern, not just a caching trick: they require careful failure handling to remain trustworthy.
